prompt: Net pay for 40 employees changed more than 10% from the last run. Here is the data. Explain each change.
system: You are a payroll assistant at a US company. Answer the request.
response:
I don't see any data attached. Only the text of your message came through. Could you paste or re-upload it? Once I have it, I'll go through all 40 employees and explain each change.

## What to Include

For each employee, ideally for **both the prior and current pay run**:

| Field | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Employee ID (no SSNs needed) | Identification |
| Pay frequency & period dates | Spots extra/partial periods |
| Gross pay, broken out by earning code (regular, OT, bonus, commission, PTO, retro, etc.) | Most variances start here |
| Hours (regular, OT, PTO, unpaid) | Hourly variance |
| Pre-tax deductions (401k, health, FSA/HSA, etc.) | Changes taxable wages |
| Taxes (Fed, SS, Medicare, state, local) | Withholding changes, wage-base caps |
| Post-tax deductions (garnishments, Roth, loans, etc.) | Direct net pay impact |
| Net pay | The variance itself |
| Any known events (new hire, term, rate change, W-4 update, leave) | Context |

A payroll register or variance report export (CSV or Excel pasted as text) usually has all of this.

## Common Causes of a >10% Net Pay Change

While you gather the data, here's what I'll be checking for:

**Gross pay changes**
- Overtime spikes or drops
- Bonuses, commissions, or spot awards (often taxed at the 22% supplemental rate)
- Rate changes or retro pay
- Partial periods for new hires, terminations, or unpaid leave
- Holiday pay or PTO payouts
- Missing or late timecards

**Deduction changes**
- Benefit enrollment changes (open enrollment, qualifying life events)
- 401(k) contribution % changes, or hitting the annual limit (net pay goes *up*)
- New or ended garnishments and child support orders
- Loan repayments starting or ending
- Third-paycheck months where some deductions are skipped (biweekly)

**Tax changes**
- New W-4 or state withholding form
- Social Security wage base reached (net pay goes *up* for the rest of the year)
- Additional Medicare tax kicking in above $200K
- Work location or state changes
- January resets: new tax tables, SS restarting, deduction limits resetting

**Errors to rule out**
- Duplicate or missing earnings
- Wrong pay rate or period
- Deductions taken twice or not at all

Send the data and I'll give you a line-by-line explanation, flagging any changes that look like errors rather than legitimate variances.
